page: Microsoft Azure M256ls_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MSMediumMemoryv4 family. Built on the x86_64 architecture with an Intel processor and operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the server provides 256 dedicated vCPUs. It is provisioned with 3892.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a memory-to-core density of 15.2 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0.0 GPUs configured.

Storage architecture on the M256ls_v4 relies entirely on external volumes, as the instance includes no local storage disks. Persistence and high IOPS workloads must be sustained via Azure Premium Storage capabilities. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring virtual network integration or dedicated IP allocation for ingress and egress traffic.

From a cost and architectural efficiency standpoint, the M256ls_v4 is positioned for consolidation of high-scale workloads into a single node rather than horizontally distributed topologies. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents an operational tradeoff, trading high-speed local scratch space for reliance on network-attached storage tiers.

The server hardware profile aligns with large-scale in-memory computing requirements. Representative workloads include massive in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, large transactional backends, and high-throughput data analytics engines requiring multi-terabyte working sets.
